rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes take people’s ingratitude to mean rejecting prophecy and its messengers, or rejecting monotheism and worshipping angels, jinn, and humans as partners.
rows.anchor: هذا ما ذكره أكثر المفسرين في معنى الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Monotheism and denying partners are independently established by reason and innate nature, so they are not a prophetic favor acquired merely by following prophets; prophets and others share this obligation.
rows.anchor: التوحيد ونفي الشركاء ليس مما يرجع فيه إلى بيان النبوة فإنه مما يستقل به العقل وتقضى به الفطرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine providence equips humanity with reason and revelation, and also preserves purified people who remain devoted to monotheism; the proof for such guides parallels the proof for prophecy because collective shirk would defeat humanity’s purpose.
rows.anchor: من الواجب في عنايته أن يجهز أفرادا منه بنفوس طاهرة وقلوب سليمة مستقيمة على فطرتها الأصلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These purified guides are prophets and Imams; their creation and mission favor them with knowledge of divine unity and remind people of truths their nature already recognizes.
rows.anchor: وهذه النفوس إن كانت فهى نفوس الأنبياء والأئمة عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Material pursuits pull people toward worldly pleasure and make them forget innate divine knowledge; without God devoted guides, creation’s purpose would fail.
rows.anchor: اشتغال الناس بالأعمال المادية ومزاولتهم للأمور الحسية تجذبهم إلى اللذات الدنيوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse means God’s guidance has kept the believers from associating anything with Him; this protection is a favor to them and to people who need reminders, yet most reject or ignore it.
rows.anchor: الحق أن تنزل الآية على هذه الحقيقة فيكون معنى الآية لم يجعل لنا بتأييد من الله سبيل إلى أن نشرك بالله شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worshippers’ gods are only names without real referents, invented by them and their ancestors; God gave no proof that they intercede or act independently.
rows.anchor: ما تعبدون من دون الله إلا أسماء خالية عن المسميات لم يضعها إلا أنتم وآباؤكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-qayyim describes a firm, capable religion that manages affairs; monotheism alone guides society toward happiness and remains true and stable.
rows.anchor: والقيم هو القائم بالأمر القوي على تدبيره أو القائم على ساقه غير المتزلزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people fail to understand monotheism because attachment to sensory life and transient worldly adornment deprives them of sound hearts and minds.
rows.anchor: لأنسهم بالحس والمحسوس وأنهماكهم في زخارف الدنيا الفانية حرموا سلامة القلب واستقامة العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human society flourishes only when its laws and livelihood rest on a true foundation matching reality, rather than a baseless fiction.
rows.anchor: هذا النوع إنما يسعد في مسير حياته إذا بنى سنن حياته وأحكام معاشه على مبنى حق مطابق للواقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two verses together form one proof for worshipping God alone: neither another self-subsisting deity nor an allegedly divinely authorized intercessor has a valid claim to worship.
rows.anchor: فقد بان من جميع ما تقدم أن الآيتين جميعا

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Baydawi, following al-Kashshaf, treats the first verse as a rhetorical case for monotheism and the second as a complete proof that alleged gods deserve no worship intrinsically or by another’s authorization.
rows.anchor: أورد البيضاوي في تفسيره تبعا للكشاف أن الآيتين تتضمنان دليلين على التوحيد

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Baydawi explains that worship is deserved intrinsically or by authorization, and neither applies to the alleged gods.
rows.anchor: قال البيضاوي وهذا من التدرج في الدعوة وإلزام الحجة بين لهم أولا رجحان التوحيد على اتخاذ الآلهة على طريق الخطابة ثم برهن على أن ما يسمونها آلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation says the one God coordinates otherwise separate causes into one coherent system, whereas multiple opposed gods would produce conflicting systems and destroy cosmic order.
rows.anchor: الله الواحد الذي يقهر بقدرته الأسباب المتفرقة التي تفعل في الكون ويسوقها على تلاؤم آثارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that reading, gods worshipped besides God are mere names: neither reason nor revelation establishes their external referents or permission to worship them.
rows.anchor: الآلهة المعبودة من دون الله أسماء لا دليل على وجود مسمياتها في الخارج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This interpretation reads the first verse in the sense of the argument that a plurality of gods in heaven and earth would cause corruption.
rows.anchor: ينزل الآية الأولى على معنى قوله تعالى لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا الأنبياء 22

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author objects that this construes the unrestricted description al-Qahhar too narrowly: God subdues every thing in its being, attributes, and effects, leaving no independent deity possible.
rows.anchor: ويرد عليه أولا أن فيه تقييدا لإطلاق قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also objects that this reading expands the second verse beyond its scope: it addresses alleged divinity by authorized intercession, not every intrinsic and derivative sense of divinity.
rows.anchor: وثانيا إن فيه تعميما لخصوص الآية الثانية من غير معمم فإن الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two predictions in this verse interpret the two prisoners’ dreams respectively: the cupbearer’s dream of pressing wine and the other prisoner’s dream of birds eating from his head.
rows.anchor: معنى الآية ظاهر، وقرينة المناسبة قاضية

rows.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام
rows.claim: An Imami report says the second prisoner admitted that he had invented his dream after hearing that he would be crucified; Joseph replied that the matter he had asked about was already decreed.
rows.anchor: ما ورد من الرواية من طرق أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام أن الثاني من الصاحبين قال له إني كذبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns in the request to remember Joseph and in the statement that he remained in prison refer to Joseph; he asked the man he expected to survive to mention his case to the king.
rows.anchor: راجعة إلى يوسف أي قال يوسف للذين ظن هو أنه سينجو منهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here zann can mean conviction rather than uncertain conjecture, as in the Qur’anic description of those who expect to meet their Lord.
rows.anchor: إطلاق الظن على مطلق الاعتقاد وله نظائر في القرآن كقوله تعالى الذين يظنون أنهم ملاقوا ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The view that Joseph interpreted the dreams only by conjecture conflicts with his declaration that the matter was settled and God’s statement that He taught him interpretation.
rows.anchor: أنه صرح لهما بعلمه في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A possible alternative makes the saved prisoner, rather than Joseph, the subject of the pronoun in the phrase about expecting rescue; the author accepts it if context allows.
rows.anchor: إلى الموصول أي قال يوسف لصاحبه الذي ظن ذلك الصاحب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns in the forgetting clause refer to the surviving cupbearer: Satan made him forget to mention Joseph to the king, so Joseph stayed imprisoned for several years.
rows.anchor: أي فأنسى الشيطان صاحبه الناجي أن يذكره لربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative that Satan made Joseph forget God and that Joseph was punished for seeking help from a person contradicts the text’s protection of the sincere and wrongly treats ordinary use of means as reliance.
rows.anchor: فمما يخالف نص الكتاب فإن الله سبحانه نص على كونه عليه السلام من المخلصين ونص على أن المخلصين لا سبيل للشيطان إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later statement that the cupbearer remembered Joseph after a lapse of years confirms that the cupbearer, not Joseph, was the one who forgot.
rows.anchor: قرينة صالحة على أن الناسي هو الساقي دون يوسف

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: In the al-Qummi report through Abu al-Jarud, the signs preceding Joseph’s imprisonment were the child’s testimony, the shirt torn from behind, and the pair racing to the door while struggling.
rows.anchor: في تفسير القمي في رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: The same report identifies the two young men as the king’s servants, a baker and a cupbearer, and says the baker had fabricated the dream and was the one crucified.
rows.anchor: ودخل معه السجن فتيان يقول عبدان للملك أحدهما خباز والآخر صاحب الشراب

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Joseph was called a benefactor because he cared for the sick, sought help for the needy, and treated fellow prisoners generously.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The al-Qummi report is textually disordered: it makes the two men royal attendants assigned to guard Joseph, which conflicts with the Qur’an’s description of them as his prison companions.
rows.anchor: أقول وفي الرواية اضطراب لفظي

rows.speaker: سماعة
rows.claim: A report in al-Ayyashi identifies Joseph’s lord in the request to remember him as the Aziz.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي عن سماعة عن قول الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says Joseph would not have remained imprisoned so long had he not uttered the request to remember him to the king.
rows.anchor: لو لم يقل يوسف الكلمة التي قال ما لبث في السجن

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A parallel report attributed to the Prophet says, God have mercy on Joseph, had he not said remember me to your lord he would not have remained imprisoned so long.
rows.anchor: عن ابن المنذر وابن أبى حاتم وابن مردويه عن أبي هريرة

rows.speaker: عكرمة والحسن
rows.claim: Similar blame of Joseph’s request is also transmitted from Ikrima, al-Hasan, and others; the author gives no grading for these reports.
rows.anchor: وروى مثله عن عكرمة والحسن وغيرهما

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report says God reminded Joseph of favors, rebuked him for seeking a creature’s help, and ordered him to remain imprisoned for several years; the author classifies it with reports contradicting the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: قال الله ليوسف ألست الذي حببتك إلى أبيك وفضلتك على الناس بالحسن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report counts Joseph’s request to the king among three alleged lapses, alongside saying the brothers were thieves and saying he had not betrayed them; it also has Gabriel rebuke him.
rows.anchor: ومثلها ما في الدر المنثور عن ابن مردويه عن ابن عباس قال عثر يوسف عليه السلام ثلاث عثرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects these reports as imputing explicit lies to the truthful Joseph and says God’s text clears him of such accusations.
rows.anchor: وفي الرواية نسبة الفرية والكذب الصريح إلى الصديق عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading that Joseph was punished for asking another person for help contradicts the text’s declaration that he was among God’s sincere servants, and using ordinary means does not imply reliance on them.
rows.anchor: والله سبحانه يبرئه من هذه المفتريات بنص كتابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage recounts Joseph’s release, rise in Egypt, and the king’s renewed investigation that fully establishes his innocence.
rows.anchor: تتضمن الآيات قصة خروجه عليه السلام من السجن ونيله عزة مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king reports his own dream to the officials; the wording may describe a repeated dream, as with the earlier prisoners’ dreams.
rows.anchor: رؤيا للملك يخبر بها الملأ والدليل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saman means fat and ʿijaf means emaciated; the latter is an exceptional feminine adjective plural, with ʿujuf offered as its regular plural.
rows.anchor: والسمان جمع سمينة والعجاف جمع عجفاء بمعنى المهزولة

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majma defines fatwa as an answer about a ruling, though it may answer about the matter itself and then is not technically a fatwa.
rows.anchor: قال في المجمع الفتيا الجواب عن حكم المعنى وقد يكون الجواب عن نفس المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʿbir comes from crossing: the interpreter passes from the dream’s familiar image to the reality represented beyond it.
rows.anchor: وهو على أي حال مأخوذ من عبور النهر ونحوه كأن العابر يعبر من الرؤيا إلى ما وراءها

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf explains that fat qualifies the cows rather than the numeral to distinguish the seven by a kind of cow; making it describe the numeral would distinguish by species and then add a second description.
rows.anchor: إذا أوقعتها صفة لبقرات فقد قصدت إلى أن تميز السبع بنوع من البقرات

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf says the dry ears must also number seven because the passage centers on seven cows and seven green ears; coordinating dry ears as a subset would conflict with the word others.
rows.anchor: الكلام مبني على انصبابه إلى هذا العدد في البقرات السمان والعجاف والسنابل الخضر

rows.speaker: الملأ
rows.claim: The officials tell the king that the vision is a jumble of dreams and that they cannot interpret this kind of mixed dream.
rows.anchor: قالوا أي قال الملأ للملك ما رأيته أضغاث أحلام وأخلاط من منامات مختلفة

rows.speaker: الملأ
rows.claim: An alternative reading is that the officials cannot interpret dreams generally, or that they know only how to interpret true dreams.
rows.anchor: أو وما نحن بتأويل جميع المنامات بعالمين وإنما نعلم تأويل الرؤى الصالحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umma here means a span of years: the period during which the cupbearer forgot to mention Joseph to his lord after Joseph asked him to do so.
rows.anchor: والمراد بها ههنا الجماعة من السنين وهى المدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The survivor is the cupbearer, who recalls Joseph’s request after years and offers to bring the interpretation of the king’s dream from him in prison.
rows.anchor: وقال الذي نجا من السجن من صاحبي يوسف فيه وادكر بعد جماعة من السنين ما سأله يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural address in I will inform you and send me includes the officials around the king, who manage affairs of state; the later reference to returning to the people supports this.
rows.anchor: تشريك لمن حضر مع الملك وهم الملأ من أركان الدولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative omits the messenger’s dispatch and arrival for concision; he calls Joseph truthful because Joseph’s accurate prior interpretations and prison conduct established that reputation.
rows.anchor: في الكلام حذف وتقدير إيجازا، والتقدير فأرسلوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cupbearer does not explicitly call the king’s vision a dream because the request to interpret it, their prior context, and the end of his speech make that clear.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر متن الرؤيا من غير أن يصرح أنه رؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first laʿalla explains the request for interpretation and the second explains the hoped-for return; returning to the people means returning with Joseph’s explanation.
rows.anchor: لعل الأول تعليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cupbearer asks on behalf of the king and officials, not for private instruction, as shown by asking for an answer to take back and by Joseph addressing the whole group.
rows.anchor: دلالة على أنه كان يستفتيه بالرسالة عن الملك والملأ ولم يكن يسأله لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people await relief from perplexity because the officials are responsible for them, or because the population is directly concerned with the king’s vision of state affairs.
rows.anchor: أن الناس كانوا في انتظار أن يرتفع بتأويله حيرتهم

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines daʾb as continued travel and, by extension, a lasting habitual practice; another reported sense is strenuous effort.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب الدأب إدامة السير دأب في السير دأبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accordingly, Joseph’s instruction is to farm continuously for seven years, either as a sustained practice or with persistent effort.
rows.anchor: وعليه فالمعنى تزرعون سبع سنين زراعة متوالية مستمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazraʿun is a report in the form of a command, emphasizing that they must comply; the following imperative to leave the harvest in its ears confirms this.
rows.anchor: وكثيرا ما يؤتى بالأمر في صورة الخبر مبالغة في وجوب الامتثال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some explain storing grain in its ears as protection from insects and spoilage, since husked and cleaned grain deteriorates faster.
rows.anchor: قيل وإنما أمر بوضعه وتركه في سنبله لأن السنبل لا يقع فيه سوس ولا يهلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shidad can mean severe because famine is hard on people, or things that attack; the latter better fits the following image of years devouring stored food.
rows.anchor: الشداد جمع شديد من الشدة بمعنى الصعوبة لما في سني الجدب والمجاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording personifies the harsh years as ravenous predators that pounce on people and consume their stored provisions.
rows.anchor: وهذا أنسب لما بعده من توصيفها بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihsan here means securing and storing a small remainder for later use.
rows.anchor: والإحصان الإحراز والادخار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yughath may mean that people are helped through relief from hardship, or that they receive rain; the next phrase about pressing makes the rain sense more apt.
rows.anchor: كان معناه ينصرون فيه من قبل الله سبحانه بكشف الكربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rain sense of yughath fits the reference to pressing; the claim that aid is more natural is unpersuasive except under a passive reading of yaʿsirun, they are rained upon.
rows.anchor: وهذا المعنى الثاني أنسب بالنظر إلى قوله بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection that Egypt’s fertility depends on Nile flooding rather than rain fails because the floodwaters are supplied by rain in Sudan.
rows.anchor: رد عليه بأن الفيضان نفسه لا يكون إلا بالمطر الذي يمده في مجاريه من بلاد السودان

rows.speaker: لسان العرب
rows.claim: The lexicon also defines ghayth as vegetation grown from rainwater, a sense that fits the following mention of pressing.
rows.anchor: قال في لسان العرب والغيث الكلاء ينبت من ماء السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pressing can mean extracting juice or oil from fruit and plants, and some interpret it as milking livestock.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يراد بالعصر الحلب أي يحلبون ضروع أنعامهم كما فسره بعضهم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final year brings crops, rain, or divine relief and abundant produce or milk; the phrasing implies plentiful blessing for people and livestock.
rows.anchor: وفيه كناية عن توفر النعمة عليهم وعلى أنعامهم ومواشيهم

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Baydawi treats the final fertile year as glad tidings beyond the interpretation of fat and lean cows; Joseph may have known it through revelation, the expected end of drought, or God’s custom of easing hardship.
rows.anchor: ولعله علم ذلك بالوحى أو بأن انتهاء الجدب بالخصب أو بأن السنة الإلهية

rows.speaker: صاحب المنار
rows.claim: The Manar author says the final year’s exceptional abundance is extra information not entailed by the dream and therefore known to Joseph through revelation.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب المنار في تفسيره في الآية والمراد أن هذا العام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says interpreters wrongly treat the dream as a forecast of seven fertile then seven barren years; Joseph instead states the required policy for surviving the anticipated famine.
rows.anchor: لم يبن كلامه على أساس إخبارهم بما سيستقبلهم من السنين السبع المخصبة ثم السنين السبع المجدبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dream depicts the practical measures the king must take for a coming famine: repeated planting, preserving grain in ears, and rationing reserves, rather than simply forecasting years.
rows.anchor: أن الذي رآه الملك من الرؤيا إنما كان مثال ما يجب عليه من اتخاذ التدبير لإنجاء الناس من مصيبة الجدب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cows represent yearly provisions: fat cows picture plentiful harvests from sustained planting, lean cows picture shortages, and their eating the fat ones pictures famine consuming saved food.
rows.anchor: فحكت السنين المخصبة والمجدبة أي الرزق الذي يرتزقون به فيها في صورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The green ears represent stores to be saved and the dry ears indicate preserving grain unthreshed; the dream shows the work required to protect food supplies.
rows.anchor: وحكت ما يجب عليهم في حفظ ذخائر الرزق بالسنبلات اليابسة قبال السنبلات الخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception allowing a little consumption is not dream interpretation but permission to use the amount needed for food during the seven productive years.
rows.anchor: ولم يزد يوسف عليه السلام في تأويله على ذلك شيئا الا أمورا ثلاثة أحدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The small amount to be preserved is a reserve and seed for the recovery year; the dream says the lean cows eat the fat ones, not that they consume every last one.
rows.anchor: وثانيها قوله { إلا قليلا مما تحصنون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final year is inferred from the repeated seven: after the seven difficult years people need not exert themselves to manage sowing and reserves.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه عليه السلام استفاده من عدد السبع الذي تكرر في البقرات السمان والعجاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph shifts from addressing the group directly to saying people will receive rain or aid and press produce, indicating they will no longer need to manage their livelihoods.
rows.anchor: ولعله لهذه الثلاثة غير السياق فقال

rows.speaker: صاحب المنار
rows.claim: The Manar author argues that the unusually specific final-year forecast cannot come from the dream and must come from revelation.
rows.anchor: أن هذا التخصيص لم يعرفه يوسف عليه السلام إلا بوحي من الله لا مقابل له في رؤيا الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dry ears are not expressly numbered because the dream depicts duties for famine management, not the famine years themselves; numbering would be needed under a forecast reading.
rows.anchor: ومما ذكرنا أيضا تظهر النكتة في ترك توصيف السنبلات اليابسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain, fodder growth, or milking livestock best fits the imagery of fat and lean cows, explaining the specific mention of rain and pressing.
rows.anchor: ومما تقدم يظهر أيضا أن الأنسب أن يكون المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the messenger reports the interpretation and advice, the king orders Joseph brought to him; the account omits that transition for brevity.
rows.anchor: وجاء الرسول وهو الساقي فنبأهم بما ذكره يوسف من تأويل الرؤيا وقال الملك بعد ما سمعه ائتوني به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king is alarmed by the predicted famine and impressed by Joseph’s practical wisdom, so he summons him to speak and understand the advice more fully.
rows.anchor: وقد أفزعه ما سمع وأدهشه ولذلك أمر بإحضاره ليكلمه ويتبصر بما يقوله مزيد تبصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The summons means release from prison for an audience, not a temporary transfer back to prison; Joseph was free to request a just inquiry before appearing.
rows.anchor: ولم يكن أمره بإتيانه به إشخاصا له بل إطلاقا من السجن وإشخاصا للتكليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph speaks courteously: he avoids naming the Aziz’s wife, asks about the women collectively, and seeks an investigation that proves his complete innocence.
rows.anchor: فلم يذكر امرأة العزيز بما يسوؤه وليس يريد إلا أن يقضي بينه وبينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His only complaint is to God in saying that his Lord knows the women’s plot; repeating Lord in his request and this statement subtly identifies the Lord addressed to the messenger.
rows.anchor: وما ألطف قوله في صدر الآية وذيلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The double use of my Lord in the request and in the statement about the women undercuts the claim that Joseph earlier called the Aziz his lord.
rows.anchor: وفيه نوع من تبليغ الحق، وليكن فيه تنبه لمن يزعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma bal asks what grave affair caused the women to cut their hands; the question prompts the king to recognize their infatuation and the exceptional difficulty of resisting them.
rows.anchor: والبال هو الأمر الذي يهتم به يقول ما هو الأمر العظيم والشأن الخطير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative omits the messenger’s return and the king’s next actions; the king summons the women and asks what happened when they pursued Joseph.
rows.anchor: جواب عن سؤال مقدر على ما في الكلام من حذف وإضمار إيجازا

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines khatb as a grave matter that draws much discussion, citing the questions to the Samaritan and to the messengers.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب الخطب الأمر العظيم الذي يكثر فيه التخاطب

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib glosses haṣḥaṣa al-haqq as the truth becoming clear through disclosure, and notes related forms of the root.
rows.anchor: وقال أيضا حصحص الحق أي وضح وذلك بانكشاف ما يظهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women’s declaration of God’s transcendence echoes their first reaction to Joseph and attests to his complete chastity and purity, just as they had marveled at his beauty.
rows.anchor: وذكرهن كلمة التنزيه { حاش لله } نظير تنزيههن حينما رأينه لأول مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Aziz’s wife admits that she pursued Joseph and that he told the truth, retracting her accusation and fully clearing him of any reciprocation.
rows.anchor: فنسبت المراودة إلى نفسها وكذبت نفسها في اتهامه بالمراودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The testimony uses layered emphasis: an indefinite wrong under negation with min, divine-transcendence language, a restrictive confession, and an emphatic nominal declaration of Joseph’s truthfulness.
rows.anchor: في قولهن، واعترافها بالذنب في سياق الحصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their statements clear Joseph of every wrong, including indecency, soliciting or responding to seduction, inclination, lying, and slander.
rows.anchor: وهذا ينفى عنه عليه السلام كل سوء أعم من الفحشاء والمراودة لها وأي ميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph says that the events establish he did not betray the Aziz in his absence and that God does not guide traitors’ schemes; this is a statement after the women’s and wife’s testimony and the king’s ruling.
rows.anchor: من كلام يوسف عليه السلام على ما يدل عليه السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an can report a speaker’s words through indirect narrative, as when the believers’ statement that they make no distinction among messengers appears within the passage about their belief.
rows.anchor: وحكاية القول كثير النظير في القرآن كقوله آمن الرسول بما أنزل إليه من ربه

rows.speaker: أحدهما عليهما السلام
rows.claim: A report transmitted in al-Ayyashi says the Prophet admired Joseph’s patience and would have required release before interpreting the king’s dream.
rows.anchor: عن أبان عن محمد بن مسلم عن أحدهما عليهما السلام قال إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the report because it either impugns Joseph’s sound strategy or suggests the Prophet would fail to show the patience he praised.
rows.anchor: وهذا النبوي لا يخلو من شيء فإن فيه أحد المحذورين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph wanted vindication, an end to the women’s pursuit, and a position from which to administer justice, not mere release; interpreting the dream first enabled the summons, and insisting on inquiry led to the king’s personal appointment.
rows.anchor: وإنما كان يريد الخروج في جو يظهر فيه براءته وتيأس منه امرأة العزيز والنسوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This was excellent statecraft: the king and officials saw Joseph’s patience, resolve, knowledge, and sound judgment, supporting his rise and public service.
rows.anchor: وهذا أحسن تدبير يتصور لما كان يبتغيه من العزة في مصر وبسط العدل والإحسان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says Gabriel reminded Joseph of a moment of desire when Joseph said he had not betrayed in secret; the author classifies it with fabricated reports contradicting the text.
rows.anchor: ففي رواية ابن عباس لما قالها يوسف

rows.speaker: حكيم بن جابر
rows.claim: A variant says Gabriel asked Joseph whether he had also been innocent when he had loosened his trousers; the source also lists similar reports from several Successors and early authorities.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية عن حكيم بن جابر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects these accusations as fabricated and contrary to the Qur’an: Joseph could not truthfully deny betrayal and then need Gabriel to expose a hidden sin.
rows.anchor: هذه وأمثالها من موضوعات الأخبار مخالفة لنص الكتاب

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf likewise condemns the claims about Joseph’s desire and undressing as fabricated reports circulated to slander God’s messenger.
rows.anchor: قال في الكشاف ولقد لفقت المبطلة روايات مصنوعة

rows.speaker: سماعة
rows.claim: A report in al-Ayyashi identifies the Aziz as Joseph’s lord in the instruction to return to him and ask about the women.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي عن سماعة قال سألته عن قول الله

rows.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report says Joseph stockpiled the harvests, sold food during famine first for money, then valuables, livestock, servants, property, and land, and finally for people’s freedom; he then freed the Egyptians and restored their possessions and kingship.
rows.anchor: سمعت الرضا عليه السلام يقول وأقبل يوسف على جمع الطعام في السبع السنين المخصبة فكبسه في الخزائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author omits many similar reports about the famine economy because most do not directly serve the interpretation of these verses.
rows.anchor: والروايات في هذا المقام كثيرة أغلبها غير مرتبطة بغرض تفسير الآيات ولذلك تركنا نقلها

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Ayyashi reports that a man may praise himself when necessary, as Joseph requested responsibility for the storehouses on the grounds that he was trustworthy and knowledgeable.
rows.anchor: قال سليمان قال سفيان قلت لأبي عبد الله عليه السلام ما يجوز أن يزكي الرجل نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous servant cited alongside Joseph is apparently Hud, who called himself a faithful adviser to his people.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن المراد بالعبد الصالح هو هود إذ يقول لقومه أبلغكم رسالات ربي وأنا لكم ناصح أمين

rows.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Rida argues that a Muslim successor may accept office under a Muslim ruler, since Joseph, a prophet, sought stewardship under Egypt’s polytheist king, whereas al-Maʾmun compelled the Imam to serve.
rows.anchor: قال فإن عزيز مصر كان مشركا وكان يوسف نبيا

rows.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Rida explains hafiz alim as guarding what is entrusted to him and knowing every language.
rows.anchor: قال حافظ على ما في يدي عالم بكل لسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph asks whether his brothers know what they did despite knowing it, to remind them of the consequences without reproaching them; describing them as ignorant supplies an excuse.
rows.anchor: إنما يخاطب المخطئ المجرم بمثل هل علمت وأتدري وأرأيت ونحوها وهو عالم بما فعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers’ emphatic question seeks an admission after signs established Joseph’s identity, rather than expressing real uncertainty.
rows.anchor: تأكيد الجملة المستفهم عنها للدلالة على أن الشواهد قامت على تحقق مضمونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph adds that Benjamin is his brother though they did not ask, because God favored both brothers, who had both been objects of envy.
rows.anchor: وإنما ألحق أخاه بنفسه ولم يسألوا عنه وما كانوا يجهلونه ليخبر عن من الله عليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph explains God’s favor through outward causes and invites his brothers to beneficence, which is realized through piety and patience.
rows.anchor: وفيه دعوتهم إلى الإحسان وبيان أنه يتحقق بالتقوى والصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ithar means choosing or preferring, and khatiʾ and mukhtiʾ both denote one who errs; the brothers acknowledge their wrongdoing and God’s preference for Joseph.
rows.anchor: الإيثار هو الاختيار والتفضيل، والخطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tathrib means reproach, excessive blame, and enumerating sins; limiting the pardon to today highlights Joseph’s magnanimous restraint when his brothers stand powerless before him.
rows.anchor: التثريب التوبيخ والمبالغة في اللوم وتعديد الذنوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph then prays for forgiveness for all the brothers who wronged him, although only some of them are present; a later statement supports their absence.
rows.anchor: ثم دعا لهم واستغفر بقوله

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: In a report from Abu Basir, Jacob’s grief over Joseph made him blind, impoverished, and physically altered; he obtained Egyptian grain twice yearly and sent sons with a small payment.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير قال سمعت أبا جعفر عليه السلام يحدث قال لما فقد يعقوب ويوسف عليهما السلام اشتد حزنه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Joseph recognized his brothers when they arrived after he became Egypt’s governor, while they failed to recognize him because of his royal status; he arranged their full ration and secretly returned their payment.
rows.anchor: فلما دخلوا على يوسف وذلك بعد ما ولاه العزيز مصر فعرفهم يوسف ولم يعرفه إخوته لهيبة الملك

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Joseph asked about Benjamin, demanded that they bring him on the next visit, and warned that they would receive no grain otherwise; the brothers promised to persuade their father.
rows.anchor: قد بلغني أنه قد كان لكم أخوان من أبيكم فما فعلا

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: The brothers found their payment returned in their bags and used it to persuade Jacob to send Benjamin, promising protection and more grain.
rows.anchor: فلما رجعوا إلى أبيهم وفتحوا متاعهم وجدوا بضاعتهم في رحالهم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: After six months, Jacob sent Benjamin with the brothers and made them swear an oath that they would return him unless they were all overwhelmed by circumstances.
rows.anchor: فلما احتاجوا بعد ستة أشهر بعثهم يعقوب وبعث معهم بضاعة يسيرة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Joseph privately embraced Benjamin, revealed his identity, and asked him to keep it secret and not grieve over what Joseph would do.
rows.anchor: فضمه إليه وبكى وقال له أنا أخوك يوسف فلا تبتئس بما تراني أعمل

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Joseph’s attendants put the king’s measure in Benjamin’s bag; after the brothers departed, Joseph’s party called them thieves and found the measure with Benjamin.
rows.anchor: جعلوا المكيال في رحل ابن يامين ففعلوا به ذلك وارتحل القوم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: The brothers pleaded for Benjamin because Jacob was elderly and invoked their oath; Joseph refused to detain anyone except the one with the measure, and the eldest stayed behind.
rows.anchor: فخذ أحدنا مكانه إنا نراك من المحسنين إن فعلت

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: The report says the brothers told Jacob that Benjamin had stolen the king’s measure and was being held, after which Jacob’s grief intensified until his back curved.
rows.anchor: قالوا ابن يامين سرق مكيال الملك فأخذه الملك بسرقته فحبس عنده

rows.speaker: أبو حمزة الثمالي
rows.claim: Abu Hamza al-Thumali reports from Abu Jaʿfar that the king’s suwaʿ was the cup from which he drank.
rows.anchor: عن أبي حمزة الثمالي عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال سمعته يقول صواع الملك الطاس الذي يشرب فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some reports instead describe the measure as a golden cup that Joseph used for measuring grain.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الروايات أنه كان قدحا من ذهب وكان يكتال به يوسف عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report explains Joseph’s statement that the caravan stole as a true indirect meaning: the brothers had stolen Joseph from his father, though they had not stolen the measure.
rows.anchor: ولقد قال يوسف أيتها العير إنكم لسارقون والله ما كانوا سرقوا وما كذب

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Kafi reports that God permits lying to reconcile; Abraham’s statement about the chief idol and Joseph’s accusation were intended to reform the situation, not to assert a falsehood.
rows.anchor: إن الله أحب اثنين وأبغض اثنين أحب الخطو فيما بين الصفين وأحب الكذب في الإصلاح

rows.speaker: رجل من أصحابنا
rows.claim: Another report from a companion of the Imams says Joseph meant that the brothers had stolen him from his father, rather than accusing them of taking the king’s cup.
rows.anchor: وفيه عن رجل من أصحابنا عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال سألت عن قول الله في يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meaning of intended reconciliation is compatible with the report that the brothers stole Joseph: the surface wording is factually inexact while the intended meaning is sound, though not understood by the hearers.
rows.anchor: قوله عليه السلام إنه أراد الإصلاح لا ينافي ما في الرواية السابقة أنه أراد به سرقهم يوسف من أبيه
